Short description: **For questions or concerns, please contact info@truthentrygard.com
Description:
1. Frame: The structural combination of the head, jambs, and sill that creates the window opening, providing support and stability to the entire window unit.
  2. Glass: The transparent or translucent sheet within a window sash frame, allowing light to enter and providing visibility while offering protection from the elements.
  3. Grilles: Decorative bars that divide window glass into smaller panes, enhancing the visual appeal of the window. Also known as muntins, grids, or windowpane dividers, grilles can be arranged in various patterns to complement different architectural styles.
  4. Head: The primary horizontal component forming the top part of a window frame, providing structural support and helping to channel water away from the window opening.
  5. Jamb: The main vertical components forming the sides of a window frame, providing structural support and helping to hold the window sash in place within the frame.
  6. Sash: A complete assembly of vertical stiles and horizontal rails, forming a frame that holds the glass pane. The sash is movable and allows for opening and closing of the window.
  7. Sill: The primary horizontal component forming the bottom part of the frame of a window, providing support and helping to prevent water infiltration into the structure.

Description: Why Use Nailing Flanges? Nailing fins or flanges, sometimes referred to as mounting flanges, are the strips of metal or plastic installed on the exterior sides of a window to mount it in place on a rough opening. Unlike a front flange which is a decorative piece of trim - a nailing flange is usually set back from the outer edge of the window frame and has fastener holes for screwing or nailing in place. The purpose of nailing fins is to anchor the window to the wall sheathing and hold it in place while the shims and screws are being installed. Fins also work in conjunction with metal and rubber flashing creating the weather resistant barrier to prevent wind and water infiltration.
